title: Visualization options and open visual assets for two static lukio sites: raw notes
method: Three research readers (diagrams and charts; animation and interactives; images, icons and open data) read primary pages, at most two tries per page; the producer queried the npm and PyPI registries, measured bundle sizes and rendered test diagrams locally. Grades: verified = read on the primary page or measured; likely = secondary source or inference; unverified = not confirmed.

package_registry_data.licence: MIT (wrapper; needs the dot binary, EPL-2.0)

bundle_size_note.note: Browser bundles measured from the jsDelivr copy of each npm file, gzip -9; only relevant when a library runs in the browser.

local_tests.note: Run locally on 2026-11-21 in a throwaway folder; nothing committed. mmdc 12.2.0 (mermaid 12.3.0) through a system Chrome via a puppeteerConfigFile with executablePath and PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1; vl-convert-python 1.9.0.post1 (reports Vega 6.2.0).

results.claim: npm install of @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 12.2.0 without the Chrome download takes about 433 MB of node_modules.

Default mmdc 12.2.0 flowchart (theme redux-color, ELK): 202 KB SVG (129 KB gzip), labels in 6 foreignObject elements, 0 SVG text elements, 4 @font-face rules with the 'Recursive Variable' font embedded as base64.
With config {htmlLabels:false, theme:'neutral', layout:'dagre', fontFamily:'system-ui, sans-serif'} the same flowchart is 18 KB (3.4 KB gzip), 0 foreignObject, labels as SVG text, no embedded font.
theme 'neutral' without htmlLabels:false still uses foreignObject (12 elements).
accTitle/accDescr produce title, desc, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and aria-roledescription in the SVG root.
Finnish letters (a/o umlauts) render correctly in flowchart, mindmap and xychart labels.
The -t (theme) flag is ignored when the -c config file sets 'theme'; a dark SVG needs its own config with theme 'dark'.
Mindmap in theme 'neutral' uses light grey boxes with white or grey text that look below 4.5:1 contrast; needs theme 'base' with themeVariables.
xychart 'line' in theme neutral draws a very pale line (poor contrast) and the y axis is numeric only, so sleep-stage names cannot be axis labels; not suitable for a hypnogram.
One run with htmlLabels:false and ELK layout hung until killed; a re-run with the same input finished, so add a timeout to the build step.
Each mmdc call starts Chrome; about 2-5 s per diagram on this machine.
mmdc has an --svgId option, needed when several SVGs are inlined on one page (default root id 'my-svg' would clash).
vl-convert-python renders a Vega-Lite step-line hypnogram to SVG in about 3 s without a browser: 10.7 KB (1.3 KB gzip), 25 text elements, no foreignObject, no external URLs.
Vega-Lite config.locale.number with decimal ',' gives Finnish decimal commas on axes (0,5).

Vega's automatic ARIA labels are English ('X-axis titled ...'); the root svg has no title/desc. Set aria:false on marks/axes or override with Finnish 'description' and wrap the SVG in a figure with a Finnish caption and data table.
A line chart needs an explicit 'order' encoding by time when the y field is ordinal; otherwise points connect in y order.

diagrams_and_charts.name: Mermaid + @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli (mmdc)

claims.claim: mermaid LICENSE file is The MIT License (MIT).
mermaid-cli is MIT.

mermaid-cli master package.json shows version 12.0.0, engines node >=22.13.0, dependency mermaid ^12.2.0, peerDependency puppeteer ^25.0.0; also bundles @fontsource fonts, katex, fontawesome, zenuml. npm 12.2.0 as stated by caller not re-checked (npmjs.com returned 403).

mmdc renders via Puppeteer + headless Chromium. To use an installed Chrome: puppeteer config JSON with executablePath, passed via --puppeteerConfigFile; set PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 at npm install to skip the browser download. Docs warn only the bundled Chromium is guaranteed.
Docker image minlag/mermaid-cli exists; reads input from /data.
README documents -i, -o, -t (theme), -b (background, e.g. transparent), --cssFile (inlined into themeCSS), --size; defers to mmdc -h for full list. The -c config-file flag is not shown in README.

HTML labels are ON by default: getEffectiveHtmlLabels returns config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart.htmlLabels ?? true. So flowchart-style labels are emitted as HTML inside <foreignObject> by default.
Root-level htmlLabels (boolean) is the supported switch; flowchart.htmlLabels is deprecated (schema default null) and root takes precedence. htmlLabels:false gives SVG <text>/<tspan> labels.
foreignObject labels disappear in non-browser SVG renderers (librsvg, Inkscape, PowerPoint, Prince); reported workaround htmlLabels false, may not fully work for all diagrams.
Clipped label text in exported SVG from font-metric mismatch / foreignObject too narrow when the viewing font differs from the measuring font.

Themes in v12 schema: default, base, dark, forest, neutral, neo, neo-dark, redux, redux-dark, redux-color, redux-dark-color. Top-level default is 'default', but flowchart and sequence override to redux-color.
Only the 'base' theme can be modified with themeVariables; darkMode variable (default false) changes derived colour calculation.

Theming docs do not mention prefers-color-scheme; one SVG has fixed colours, so render twice (light/dark) or override colours with CSS (themeCSS / --cssFile with CSS custom properties, works when SVG is inlined).

accTitle: single line; accDescr: single line or accDescr { multi-line }. Output: <title> and <desc> children of svg, aria-labelledby / aria-describedby on svg, aria-roledescription = diagram type. Available for all diagram types.

Flowchart: wrap unicode text in double quotes; markdown strings auto-wrap long text (markdownAutoWrap:false disables); ELK is default layout in v12 (layout: dagre for old); defaultRenderer removed in v12.
flowchart wrappingWidth default 120.
Mindmap: markdown strings auto-wrap; tidy-tree layout option; ::icon() experimental and needs icon fonts supplied by the site (self-host).
xychart: docs use keyword 'xychart' (one legend example still shows xychart-beta); multi-word text must be quoted; labelRotation for x-axis; no wrapping or a11y notes.
Sankey keyword is 'sankey' (no beta label in docs); CSV rows source,target,value; quote text with commas.

No Mermaid issue found specifically about Finnish/umlaut characters; text is measured in real Chromium so a-umlaut/o-umlaut are fine if the same font is used when viewing; risk is clipping when page font differs.
timeline, pie, quadrantChart, block, kanban pages not individually checked in this pass.

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: Node >=22 + Puppeteer + headless Chrome (large download, or system Chrome via executablePath). Python: subprocess.run(['mmdc','-i',src,'-o',out_svg,'-c',config_json,'-t',theme,'-b','transparent','--puppeteerConfigFile',pcfg]). Batch diagrams to avoid repeated Chrome start-up. Put htmlLabels:false in config JSON.
diagrams_and_charts.a11y: accTitle/accDescr -> /<desc> + aria-labelledby/aria-describedby. Default foreignObject labels are HTML inside SVG; htmlLabels:false gives SVG text. Inline the SVG (not <img>) so screen readers reach text; add a text alternative for complex diagrams.
diagrams_and_charts.no_js_print: Static SVG, no JS. Browser printing fine; non-browser converters may drop foreignObject labels -> use htmlLabels:false.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: Fixed colours per render. (a) render twice and switch with <picture><source media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'> or CSS tied to the site toggle; (b) one render + --cssFile mapping fills/strokes to site CSS custom properties (inline SVG only).
diagrams_and_charts.phone: Wide flowcharts shrink badly; prefer TD direction, short labels, scrollable figure wrapper, useMaxWidth. Long Finnish compounds need explicit breaks or markdown strings.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Strong for flowcharts, cycles, mindmaps, timelines; plain text in Markdown. Heavy build dependency (Chrome).

diagrams_and_charts.name: Graphviz (dot) + Python graphviz + WASM builds
diagrams_and_charts.licence: Graphviz EPL-2.0 (https://graphviz.org/license/); Python graphviz MIT; @hpcc-js/wasm Apache-2.0; @viz-js/viz MIT (bundled Graphviz code remains EPL-2.0)

claims.claim: Graphviz is licensed under Eclipse Public License v2.0.
Python package graphviz is MIT and needs the Graphviz dot binary on PATH to render; svg is a supported format.
hpcc-js-wasm monorepo is Apache-2.0, includes @hpcc-js/wasm-graphviz and wasm-graphviz-cli; for Node and browsers; graphviz.dot() returns SVG.
viz-js LICENSE is MIT (Michael Daines); text does not mention Graphviz EPL.
Compiled Graphviz inside the WASM packages stays under EPL-2.0.
Graphviz SVG output uses real <text> elements plus <title> per node/edge.

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: subprocess ['dot','-Tsvg',in,'-o',out] (system package, no browser), or graphviz.Source(src).pipe(format='svg'), or Node WASM without system install.
diagrams_and_charts.a11y: Real <text>; add <title>/<desc>/role in post-processing; no accTitle equivalent.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: Colours fixed in DOT; render twice or post-process to CSS classes/currentColor; bgcolor=transparent.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Good for graphs; harder syntax than Mermaid; no mindmap/timeline/charts.

diagrams_and_charts.name: D2 (terrastruct/d2)

claims.claim: Open source under Mozilla Public License 2.0 (Copyright 2022 Terrastruct).
Install via install script or go install; ships Source Sans Pro as default font.
CLI flags: --theme/-t (D2_THEME), --dark-theme (D2_DARK_THEME, used when viewer's browser is in dark mode; explicit styles in D2 code still apply), --layout/-l default dagre, --pad, --font-regular.
With a dark theme set, the SVG CSS includes @media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){...}, so one SVG follows OS preference (not a manual site toggle).
Docs: dark themes not set by default; with the flag set the diagram switches when system preference is dark.
SVG renderer writes labels as <text> and embeds fonts via @font-face inside the SVG (self-contained, larger files); Markdown blocks historically used foreignObject.
Layouts: dagre default, ELK available; TALA is closed-source, paid for commercial use, watermark without licence.
README says nothing about accessibility.

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: Single Go binary, no browser for SVG. subprocess ['d2','--theme','0','--dark-theme','200','--layout','elk','in.d2','out.svg'].
diagrams_and_charts.a11y: Real <text>; no documented title/desc syntax - post-process.
diagrams_and_charts.no_js_print: Static SVG; dark media query is screen-only so print stays light.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: Best built-in: one SVG with light + prefers-color-scheme dark. Manual site toggle needs post-processing.
diagrams_and_charts.phone: Embedded fonts keep metrics consistent; wide diagrams need scroll wrapper.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Nice output; new syntax; no charts/timelines; avoid TALA.

diagrams_and_charts.name: PlantUML
diagrams_and_charts.licence: Multi-licence jars: GPL (recommended), GPLv2, LGPL, Apache-2.0, BSD, EPL-2.0, MIT (https://plantuml.com/download)

claims.claim: Download page offers GPL, GPL v2, LGPL, ASL, BSD, EPL 2.0 and MIT jars (v1.2026.10); non-GPL builds lack some features (e.g. Ditaa); ELK only in EPL build; GPL builds embed Graphviz.
Requires a Java runtime.
Public server gets the diagram source encoded in the URL; self-hosting possible (Tomcat 10 war or local PicoWeb server).
-tsvg output uses <text> elements.

diagrams_and_charts.a11y: Text as <text>; no verified title/desc support.

diagrams_and_charts.name: Kroki

claims.claim: MIT licence; self-host with docker run yuzutech/kroki; companions kroki-mermaid, kroki-bpmn, kroki-excalidraw, kroki-diagramsnet.

Public kroki.io at build time sends diagram source to a third party (build-time privacy issue, not runtime).

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: HTTP POST from Python to a local Docker container; mermaid companion still runs headless Chrome.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Overkill for two sites; do not use the public instance.

diagrams_and_charts.name: Vega-Lite + vl-convert-python

claims.claim: Vega-Lite LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause (UW Interactive Data Lab).
VlConvert is BSD 3-Clause; embeds Vega/Vega-Lite in an embedded V8 runtime; no browser or Node.js; CLI vl2svg; Python vlc.vegalite_to_svg(spec).
Bundled libraries need no network; remote data/images/Google Fonts only if configured; Google Fonts opt-in; system fonts plus extra font dirs.
Vega scenegraph generates role, aria-roledescription and aria-label attributes for marks and guides (description feeds aria-label).
Vega SVG renderer writes labels as <text>.

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: pip install vl-convert-python (wheel with embedded V8); in-process call vlc.vegalite_to_svg(spec_dict) from the Python build.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: config colours in spec; render twice or post-process to CSS vars.
diagrams_and_charts.phone: Pick modest width; SVG scales via viewBox.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Best fit for data charts in a Python build.

diagrams_and_charts.name: Observable Plot

claims.claim: LICENSE is ISC.
document option allows a virtual DOM implementation for server-side rendering in Node (e.g. jsdom).
Marks support ariaLabel, ariaDescription, ariaHidden; title/subtitle/caption wrap SVG in an HTML figure.
Axes use currentColor so inline SVG follows site text colour.

diagrams_and_charts.build_step: Node script with jsdom via subprocess.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: currentColor helps; series colours via CSS.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Good, but adds Node+jsdom; vl-convert simpler.

claims.claim: LICENSE.md is The MIT License.
Canvas only; accessibility via role=img, aria-label and fallback content inside <canvas>; docs do not mention SVG.

diagrams_and_charts.name: Apache ECharts (SSR SVG)

claims.claim: LICENSE is Apache 2.0; lists d3 BSD-3-Clause subcomponents.
Server-side: init(null, null, {renderer:'svg', ssr:true, width, height}); setOption; renderToSVGString(); zero-dependency (no jsdom/canvas); animation via embedded CSS, disable with animation:false.
zrender SVG backend creates <text> nodes.
aria component: auto description, custom aria.description, decal patterns for non-colour distinction; sets role=img and aria-label on the container DOM.
In SSR string mode there is no container DOM, so aria-label may be missing from the SVG string.

diagrams_and_charts.a11y: <text> labels; decals help colour-blind users; pair with table.

diagrams_and_charts.name: matplotlib (SVG backend)
diagrams_and_charts.licence: Matplotlib License, PSF-based, BSD-compatible (https://matplotlib.org/stable/project/license.html); SPDX id not stated on page

claims.claim: Licence is based on the PSF license; Matplotlib only uses BSD-compatible code.
svg.fonttype default 'path' (glyphs as paths); 'none' keeps text as text, assumes fonts installed at view time.
svg.hashsalt fixed string gives reproducible SVG ids.

diagrams_and_charts.a11y: With svg.fonttype='none' text is <text>; post-process title/desc/role; pair with table.
diagrams_and_charts.theming: Style sheets; render twice or post-process colours.
diagrams_and_charts.teaching_fit: Good if data lives in Python.

animation_and_interactives.name: CSS animation + prefers-reduced-motion
animation_and_interactives.licence: Platform feature (no licence); own CSS under site CC BY 4.0

claims.claim: prefers-reduced-motion has values no-preference and reduce; Baseline widely available since Jan 2020
MDN example swaps a scaling animation for a gentler opacity change under reduce
WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide is Level A: auto-starting motion lasting over 5 s in parallel with other content needs pause/stop/hide
2.2.2 is met if the motion stops by itself within 5 s (G11, G152) or a control stops it (G4, G186)
2.3.3 Animation from Interactions is Level AAA (not required for AA); technique C39 = CSS prefers-reduced-motion, SCR40 = JS matchMedia
CSS animations and the reduced-motion media query work with JavaScript disabled
Print shows a static state; an @media print rule with animation:none gives a deterministic, chosen frame

animation_and_interactives.a11y: Good if the loop ends within 5 s or a visible pause control exists (needs JS, so default to a static or finished state and let JS add play/pause). Always honour reduce. Animated content also needs a text or table equivalent.
animation_and_interactives.no_js_print: Runs without JS. Pause control needs JS (or a CSS-only checkbox). Safer: single iteration that ends on the meaningful frame, or start paused. Add @media print {animation:none} so print shows the final frame.
animation_and_interactives.phone: Cheap when animating transform/opacity; fine on old phones.
animation_and_interactives.teaching_fit: Best fit for both pilots: hypnogram line drawing (stroke-dashoffset) and slow ring rotation (transform: rotate).
animation_and_interactives.worth_it_when: Default choice whenever motion is a simple reveal or emphasis; zero dependency weight.

animation_and_interactives.name: SVG SMIL (animate, animateTransform)

claims.claim: <animate> is Baseline widely available since Jan 2020; MDN page has no deprecation notice
MDN advises a way to pause/disable animation and respecting prefers-reduced-motion
SMIL does not respect prefers-reduced-motion by itself; must be gated by CSS/JS or kept to a finite repeatCount
SMIL in an SVG loaded via img still animates but page CSS cannot reach it to stop it

animation_and_interactives.a11y: Harder to honour reduced motion than CSS. Prefer CSS keyframes on inline SVG; use SMIL only with finite duration under 5 s.
animation_and_interactives.no_js_print: Runs without JS. Printed frame may be mid-animation (likely); use fill=freeze and short dur.
animation_and_interactives.teaching_fit: Possible for hypnogram, but CSS stroke animation is simpler and controllable.
animation_and_interactives.worth_it_when: Only for attribute animation CSS cannot do (e.g. path morphing) in a standalone SVG asset.

animation_and_interactives.name: D3
animation_and_interactives.licence: ISC (LICENSE: Copyright 2010-2026 Mike Bostock); npm d3 7.9.2
animation_and_interactives.self_hostable: yes; best used at build time only (zero runtime JS)

claims.claim: LICENSE text is ISC, copyright Mike Bostock
npm latest d3 is 7.9.2 with licence ISC
D3 is split into submodules (d3-array, d3-scale, d3-shape...) importable separately
Most modules (d3-scale, d3-array, d3-format) do not touch the DOM; d3-selection/transition/axis do
DOM-free modules can produce SVG path strings in Node at build time; selections would need jsdom

animation_and_interactives.a11y: Output is plain SVG: we control title/desc, roles and the text table.
animation_and_interactives.no_js_print: Built-time output is static SVG: prints, works without JS.
animation_and_interactives.teaching_fit: Good geometry helpers (d3-shape curveStep for hypnogram, arc/pie for rings), but the Python engine can compute the same.
animation_and_interactives.worth_it_when: Only if a Node build step is acceptable and there are many charts; for 1-2 diagrams Python-generated SVG is lighter.

animation_and_interactives.name: three.js
animation_and_interactives.licence: MIT (LICENSE: Copyright 2010-2026 three.js authors); npm three 0.187.0
animation_and_interactives.self_hostable: yes - copy build/three.module.js (+ examples/jsm addons) and map with an importmap; no CDN required

claims.claim: LICENSE is MIT
npm latest three is 0.187.0, MIT
WebGPURenderer uses WebGPU when available, otherwise a WebGL 2 backend; forceWebGL option exists
WebGL 1.0 global support about 97.57%
WebGL 2.0 global support about 97.29%; iOS Safari supported from 15, disabled by default 12-14.8
Self-hosting via importmap to local three.module.js (manual page unreadable; general practice)
Canvas output has no accessibility tree; needs aria-label/fallback and text equivalent

animation_and_interactives.a11y: None by default. Needs role=img + label, static SVG/text equivalent, keyboard controls if interactive, reduced-motion gating in JS.
animation_and_interactives.no_js_print: Nothing without JS; canvas prints blank or a stale frame. Ship a static image in the HTML and hide canvas in print.
animation_and_interactives.phone: About 3% of users lack WebGL; heavy download and GPU/battery cost on old phones; feature-detect and fall back to a static image.
animation_and_interactives.teaching_fit: Poor for both pilots (2D). 3D body/organ models also clash with picture rules.
animation_and_interactives.worth_it_when: Only for genuinely 3D content (e.g. a rotatable molecule) that SVG cannot convey.

animation_and_interactives.name: p5.js
animation_and_interactives.licence: LGPL-2.1 (license.txt in repo); npm p5 2.4.0 licence LGPL-2.1

npm latest p5 is 2.4.0, licence LGPL-2.1

animation_and_interactives.no_js_print: Nothing without JS; needs static fallback.
animation_and_interactives.phone: Library is large (likely several hundred kB minified); default draw loop drains battery unless noLoop().
animation_and_interactives.teaching_fit: Good for student coding of generative sketches; overkill for teacher diagrams.
animation_and_interactives.worth_it_when: Only if students write sketches themselves.
